summary: The Windows installer compiles again after the previous fix exposed a second Inno Setup Pascal Script incompatibility: `ISCC` aborted with "Unknown identifier 'Randomize'" because Inno's scripting engine does not expose `Randomize`. The installer generates the first-run admin password with a random draw, so the release `windows-installer` job failed and `mymatasan-setup-<version>-windows-x64.exe` was again not built. Inno's own `Random` is unusable here regardless: it is backed by Delphi's global `RandSeed` (initialised to 0) that the script cannot seed, so every install would have produced the identical bootstrap password. The password generator now uses a self-contained LCG seeded from the install-time `GetTickCount` (perturbed by the wall-clock time of day), so it both compiles and yields a distinct one-time admin password per install.
compatibility: Backward compatible — installer behavior and finish-page UX are unchanged. The generated bootstrap admin password is still a 16-character, must-change-on-first-login credential; only its randomness source changed (and is now actually seeded). Portable archive, `.deb`/`.rpm`, and Docker artifacts were unaffected.
